verses.text: On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel;
and he said to Aaron, “Take a calf from the herd for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering, without defect, and offer them before Yahweh.
You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering; and a calf and a lamb, both a year old, without defect, for a burnt offering;
and a bull and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before Yahweh; and a meal offering mixed with oil: for today Yahweh appears to you.’”
They brought what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting: and all the congregation came near and stood before Yahweh.
Moses said, “This is the thing which Yahweh commanded that you should do: and Yahweh’s glory shall appear to you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Draw near to the altar, and offer your sin offering, and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself, and for the people; and offer the offering of the people, and make atonement for them; as Yahweh commanded.”
So Aaron came near to the altar, and killed the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.
The sons of Aaron presented the blood to him; and he dipped his finger in the blood, and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar:
but the fat, and the kidneys, and the cover from the liver of the sin offering, he burned upon the altar; as Yahweh commanded Moses.
The meat and the skin he burned with fire outside the camp.
He killed the burnt offering; and Aaron’s sons delivered the blood to him, and he sprinkled it around on the altar.
They delivered the burnt offering to him, piece by piece, and the head: and he burned them upon the altar.
He washed the innards and the legs, and burned them on the burnt offering on the altar.
He presented the people’s offering, and took the goat of the sin offering which was for the people, and killed it, and offered it for sin, like the first.
He presented the burnt offering, and offered it according to the ordinance.
He presented the meal offering, and filled his hand from there, and burned it upon the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning.
He also killed the bull and the ram, the sacrifice of peace offerings, which was for the people: and Aaron’s sons delivered to him the blood, which he sprinkled around on the altar,
and the fat of the bull and of the ram, the fat tail, and that which covers the innards, and the kidneys, and the cover of the liver:
and they put the fat upon the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar:
and the breasts and the right thigh Aaron waved for a wave offering before Yahweh, as Moses commanded.
Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people, and blessed them; and he came down from offering the sin offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting, and came out, and blessed the people: and Yahweh’s glory appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from before Yahweh, and consumed the burnt offering and the fat upon the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted, and fell on their faces.

footnotes.content: The eighth day—a fresh beginning, a turning point. Aaron steps into his calling before all Israel's eyes. I notice how the Lord marks new seasons with witnesses: not hidden, not ashamed, but gathered and seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A calf for sin offering, a ram for burnt offering—each without defect. The holiness we offer must cost us something real, not the leftovers. That's how we show we mean it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people bring their own gifts too: a goat, a calf, a lamb, all yearlings, all perfect. When the priest enters his office, the people don't stand idle—they move with him, joining their worship to his.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Today Yahweh appears to you'—the priest and people both hold their breath. This isn't routine; this is covenant made visible. The meal offering mixed with oil speaks of gladness too, not only awe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They brought it all. No delays, no doubts. And they stood before Yahweh—gathered, expectant, ready. There's something in that standing together that steadies the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses sets the promise: Yahweh's glory shall appear. Not maybe. Shall. When we've done what the Lord commands, His answer comes. I've seen it happen over and over.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron is told to make atonement for himself first, then for the people. The priest's own sin must be addressed; he cannot carry unforgiven guilt into the holy place. Honesty comes before intercession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron came near to the altar and killed the calf. The work is real—blood, death, sacrifice. He takes the responsibility in his own hands. No hiding from what holiness requires.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His sons present the blood to him; he dips his finger and marks the altar's horns. Blood on the horns—the sign of a covenant kept, a life given, a boundary honored. Every horn speaks of the Lord's reach and rule.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat, the kidneys, the liver cover—what the Lord commanded is what Aaron burns. No shortcuts, no innovations. Obedience in the small details is how we honor Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The meat and skin burned outside the camp—removed, separated, taken from the holy place. The sin offering carries away what cannot remain in God's presence. Mercy and holiness both act here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the burnt offering—entirely consumed, nothing held back. Aaron's sons deliver the blood to him with each piece, each step deliberate. The whole is offered; the whole is received.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Piece by piece, the burnt offering goes to the flames: legs, head, entrails. Complete, methodical, nothing wasted. The Lord sees what is offered and honors the whole heart that brings it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He washed the innards and legs—cleanliness in the midst of blood and offering. Even in the work of sacrifice, there is order and care. The Lord loves beauty and reverence together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people's goat came next, Aaron's hands now lifted to intercede for them. He knows their names, their burdens. The priest stands in the gap, and the Lord honors it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The burnt offering according to ordinance—no deviation. When we move toward the Lord's altar, the path is clear and narrow. We follow not because we are afraid, but because we trust He knows the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The meal offering, fine flour and oil, a handful burned on the altar. Grain, not blood—a different language of thanks. The Lord accepts all sincere gifts, speaks all our dialects of love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bull and ram for peace offerings—now the people's portion draws near. Not only sin covered and devotion given, but peace—shalom—peace meals shared between the people and their God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fat of bull and ram, the tail, the covering, the kidneys—each part has meaning, each part is seen and honored. Nothing is careless in the Lord's house; everything spoken for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat laid on the breasts—placed where the heart is, where feeling runs deepest. The Lord claims not just our obedience but our affection, not just the ritual but the love beneath it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron waves the breasts and right thigh—the wave offering, lifted up and set apart. His hands lift toward heaven what the people have brought; their gifts rise with his prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron lifts his hands toward the people and blesses them. He comes down from the altar, the offering complete, and his very presence now carries a blessing. The work of priesthood is intercession made flesh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses and Aaron entered the Tent together, came out, and blessed the people. The priestly work is done; now comes the answer. All Israel watched and waited, and now the Lord Himself steps into the scene.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed the burnt offering and the fat. The people shouted and fell on their faces. Readers today hear an echo: the Lord Himself saying yes—I see you, I accept this gift, I am here. The fire that fell then speaks to the Holy Spirit who dwells in us now, sealing us as His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
